items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Duke Ellington, Thelonious Monk, there’s so much out there. ... Duke always hated that too

ctx.x: And you seem to have a knack for finding tunes maybe that are not played to death.

Well again it comes down to my own boredom threshold. You know George Gershwin is a great composer, but the man wrote hundreds and hundreds of songs. You don’t always have to play “Lady Be Good,” and “Someone to Watch Over Me.” There’s all kinds of songs the man wrote. Duke Ellington, Thelonious Monk, there’s so much out there. And again, like a song like this, I just try to listen to it and say what can I lend to this song.
Now this section here, it’s almost like you guys are both soloing at the same time.
